To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CNNs can learn to recognize people based on their way of walking from sequences of low-level motion features.

(i) CNNs trained with optical flow cuboids can achieve state-of-the-art gait recognition performance; (ii) CNNs can learn gait signatures from low resolution images; and, finally, (iii) CNNs are capable of learning gait signatures without the need of hand-crafted motion features.

(1) the proposed CNN architecture can learn high-level gait signatures from low-level motion data, (2) the use of spatio-temporal optical flow cuboids as input data to CNN allows to obtain very compact gait signatures (i.e. with a resolution 8 times lower than previously reported results) and (3) the proposed CNN gait signature is invariant to changes in the walking speed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
automatic learning of gait signatures for people identification from video sequences.

CNNs can be effectively used for gait analysis, and that optical flow is a suitable feature for the task.
